answer: Cross-Epoch Nectar Drift Lock. Each identity’s daily behavioral fingerprint (transaction timing, counterparty mix, value distribution) is hashed into a violet vector; epochs compare current vectors to the prior three, and drift beyond a calibrated threshold freezes rewards pending review. Sybils must maintain consistent histories across many identities, so an attacker pays sustained coordination cost per identity—continuous genuine-looking activity for at least three epochs—before reaching the zenith of reward eligibility, making mass fake identities economically unfavorable.
